events.label: birth
events.text: Born Prince Alexander Albert Victor of Battenberg at Windsor Castle.

evidence.quote: born Prince Alexander Albert Victor of Battenberg ; 23 November 1886
Prince Alexander was born in 1886 at Windsor Castle in Berkshire

events.text: Styled His Highness by royal warrant of Queen Victoria.

evidence.quote: on 13 December 1886 , he was styled His Highness under a Royal Warrant

events.label: baptism
events.text: Baptised at Windsor Castle; godparents included Queen Victoria.

evidence.quote: He was baptised in the White Drawing Room of Windsor Castle on 18 December 1886

events.text: Began service in the Royal Navy.

evidence.quote: He served in the Royal Navy from 1902 to 1908

events.text: Passed qualifying examination to become Royal Navy service cadet.

evidence.quote: passed a qualifying examination to become service cadet in the Royal Navy in March 1902

events.text: Joined cadet training ship HMS Britannia at Dartmouth.

evidence.quote: joined the cadet training ship HMS Britannia at Dartmouth on 8 May 1902

events.text: Ended service in the Royal Navy.

evidence.quote: He served in the Royal Navy from 1902 to 1908

events.text: Joined the British Army.

evidence.quote: In 1909 , he joined the British Army

events.text: Appointed Second Lieutenant (on probation), Grenadier Guards.

evidence.quote: being appointed Second Lieutenant ( on probation ) in the Grenadier Guards on 4 August 1909

events.text: Became one of the earliest members of The Castaways Club.

evidence.quote: in 1910 , became one of the earliest members of The Castaways Club

events.text: Confirmed in the rank of Second Lieutenant.

evidence.quote: He was confirmed in the rank on 22 November 1911

events.text: Promoted to Lieutenant.

evidence.quote: and was promoted to Lieutenant on 15 August 1913

events.text: Seconded to the staff as extra aide-de-camp.

evidence.quote: He was seconded to the staff to act as an extra aide-de-camp on 10 April 1915

events.text: Promoted to captain (seniority date)

evidence.quote: ranking as a Captain with seniority of 15 July 1915

events.label: honour
events.text: Authorised to wear insignia of the Russian Order of St Vladimir.

evidence.quote: On 1 June 1917 , he was authorised to wear the insignia of the Russian Order of St Vladimir

events.text: Married Lady Irene Denison at the Chapel Royal, St James's Palace.

evidence.quote: On 19 July 1917 , he married Lady Irene Denison

events.text: Created Marquess of Carisbrooke, Earl of Berkhamsted and Viscount Launceston.

evidence.quote: On 7 November 1917 , he was created Marquess of Carisbrooke , Earl of Berkhamsted and Viscount Launceston

events.text: Resigned his commission in the British Army.

evidence.quote: He resigned his commission on 19 June 1919

events.label: birth of daughter

evidence.quote: Lady Iris Mountbatten ( 13 January 1920 – 1 September 1982 )

events.text: Commissioned as acting pilot officer in the RAF.

evidence.quote: joined the Royal Air Force and was commissioned an acting pilot officer on 6 June 1941

events.text: Regraded as pilot officer (on probation).

evidence.quote: On 6 August , he was regraded as a pilot officer ( on probation )

events.text: Confirmed in his rank of pilot officer.

evidence.quote: He was confirmed in his rank on 6 June 1942

events.text: Promoted to flying officer (war-substantive).

evidence.quote: was promoted to flying officer ( war-substantive ) on 6 August 1942

evidence.quote: Lady Irene Denison ( 4 July 1890 – 16 July 1956 )

events.label: death
events.text: Died at Kensington Palace, aged 73.

evidence.quote: 23 November 1886 – 23 February 1960
Lord Carisbrooke , died in 1960 , aged 73 , at Kensington Palace

events.text: Title Marquess of Carisbrooke became extinct upon his death.

evidence.quote: 23 November 1886 – 23 February 1960

undated_mentions: Educated at the Britannia Royal Naval College
Battenberg family took surname Mountbatten; became Sir Alexander Mountbatten
Staff officer attached to Air Chief Marshal Sir Trafford Leigh-Mallory during WWII
Began career as entry-level clerk at Lazard Brothers bankers
Worked for a company that oversaw housing estates
Took control of social work for the tenants
Became director of Lever Brothers and several other corporations
Ashes buried in the Battenberg Chapel, St Mildred's Church, Whippingham
